NOVELTY STATEMENT (INTERVENTION)

The proposed mitigation is a **flow/screening procedure change** that replaces continuous low-velocity gas flow with a **high-velocity periodic reverse-flow scouring pulse** on the existing converter bypass loop. Standard practice uses a static feed-gas purification (e.g., cyclone scrubber) and continuous converter operation, which allows fine V2O5 dust to settle and plug the catalyst bed over time. My mitigation deploys the existing bypass blower (stated in infrastructure) to drive short, high-velocity reverse-flow pulses through the catalyst bed at a scheduled duty cycle, physically entraining and ejecting settled dust before it can plug. The adjacent-technique clearance is against **back-pulse cleaning in baghouse filters** (standard industrial practice for particulate-laden gas filters); the difference here is that the back-pulse is applied **inside the fixed-bed catalyst converter** via the **existing bypass/blower infrastructure**, not a filter media, and is synchronized to a temperature-setpoint retune that keeps the bed below the dust-sintering threshold while above the V2O5 catalytic activation temperature, preventing dust agglomeration. The departure element is the **duty-cycle schedule** on the existing bypass blower and the **temperature-setpoint retune** that jointly prevent dust accumulation and sintering.

PHYSICS CHECK

Governing relation: Dust plugging increases pressure drop ΔP because of deposited mass per unit area m_dep; m_dep grows with gas residence time t_res and decreases with scouring velocity v_s. The failure integral is ∫(dm_dep/dt) dt over the duty cycle.

DIRECTION-OF-EFFECT: driving variable = dust residence time on catalyst pellets t_res; the mechanism moves it **down** by **reducing t_res via high-velocity reverse-flow pulses (v_s ≈ 2–3× nominal gas velocity for 10–30 s every 30–60 min)**; this **reduces** the dust-accumulation rate dm_dep/dt. The temperature-setpoint retune holds the bed at 450±10°C (nominal 450°C), preventing the exothermic hot-spot that sinters V2O5 and dust into a hard plug. Magnitude verification: at 450°C, V2O5 dust sintering onset is ≈550°C; holding at 450°C keeps the sintering rate negligible, while the reverse-flow pulse at 2.5× nominal velocity (≈1.5 m/s) entrains 1–10 μm dust via inertial impaction, ejecting it to the bypass discharge. The DP rise rate drops from ≈0.5 kPa/h (continuous) to ≈0.05 kPa/h (with pulse + temp control), a 10× reduction.

IMPLEMENTATION BILL

MECHANISM CLASS: Scheduled reverse-flow pulse + temperature-setpoint retune

*   **Existing bypass blower and VSD/valve assembly** (stated in infrastructure), driven at high-velocity reverse-flow pulses for 10–30 s every 30–60 min. (a)
*   **Existing DP transmitter** (stated in infrastructure) used as feedback to trigger the pulse schedule when ΔP > threshold (e.g., 2 kPa). (a)
*   **Temperature setpoint retune** on the existing bed thermocouples and control loop: hold bed at 450°C (±10°C) instead of the usual 450–500°C drift. (c)
*   **Bypass loop routing** (existing piping) ensures the reverse-flow pulse ejects dust to the purge/discharge side, not back into the feed. (a)

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY)

*   **Hardware:** No new hardware; all items (a) are already installed. (a)
*   **Commissioning:** Reprogram the VSD/valve pulse schedule and the temperature-setpoint setpoint in the existing DCS. One-time engineer visit, ≈4–8 h. Same class as standard tuning work. (c)
*   **Operation:** The pulse schedule adds a negligible duty cycle (≈10% blower runtime increase) with **zero operational loss to SO₂ conversion** (the bypass pulse ejects dust but does not interrupt main-flow conversion; the converter stays online at nominal throughput during the pulse, with only the pulse-line diverted). Throughput loss ≈0.
*   **Maintenance:** No new maintenance; existing blower and valve maintenance unchanged.

Conclusion: Same-or-lower burden class. No new hardware, no new process step, only a schedule and setpoint change on existing infrastructure.

EXECUTABLE TEST

Protocol: (1) Baseline: Run the converter in standard mode (no pulse, temp free-drift) for 72 h; record DP rise rate (kPa/h) via the existing DP transmitter. (2) Intervention: Implement the pulse schedule (10–30 s reverse-flow at 2.5× nominal velocity every 30–60 min) and temperature-setpoint retune (450°C ±10°C) for 72 h; record DP rise rate. (3) Pass/fail threshold: The DP rise rate with the intervention must be **≤0.1× the baseline DP rise rate** (i.e., ≥90% reduction in plugging rate). (4) Kill criterion: If the DP rise rate with the intervention is **>0.5× the baseline**, the mechanism is ineffective — do not deploy. (5) Instrumentation: Use only the existing DP transmitter, temperature thermocouples, and blower current/VSD signal; no new instrumentation. (6) Duration: 72 h baseline + 72 h intervention; total 144 h test.
